panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Low-power H&E of NXG skin biopsy showing diffuse dermal to subcutis mononuclear / foamy histiocytic infiltration, consistent with NXG in NXG case report. b: H&E shows palisaded granuloma with necrobiosis, classic NXG histology supported by in-text palisaded granulomas surrounding large necrobiotic areas. c: High-power H&E shows xanthoma / foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells, plus visible wreath-like Touton cell, diagnostic for NXG. d: High-power H&E shows cholesterol clefts in center of necrobiotic area, classic NXG feature confirmed by in-text mention.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E of the periorbital biopsy showing broad zones of necrobiotic altered collagen under a normal epidermis, described in the caption of a biopsy consistent with NBX. B: H&E at 20x showing zonal altered collagen (necrobiosis) rimmed by a mixed inflammatory infiltrate, a classic granulomatous pattern in NBX periorbital biopsy. C: High-power H&E showing foamy macrophages and giant cells at the edge of necrobiotic collagen, a hallmark xanthogranulomatous finding in NBX. D: Second 40x field showing foamy macrophages and giant cells at the necrobiosis border, consistent with the NBX diagnosis of the periorbital biopsy.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal T2 MRI of a patient with biopsy/clinically diagnosed NXG-associated orbital disease showing superior orbital soft tissue pressing the globe downward; caption and in-text mention explicitly link the mass to the NXG case (Figure 1). Imaging manifestation is a recognized but less common (variant) orbital presentation of NXG rather than the classic periorbital plaques; no vocabulary finding key covers globe compression, so it is proposed. B: B-scan ultrasound of the right orbit showing flattening of the superior scleral contour from external compression by the NXG orbital mass described in the caption and in-text passage (orbital ultrasonography demonstrated superior compression of the globe). Same patient and disease as panel A; variant orbital manifestation of NXG, with no matching vocabulary finding key.
